patch.sql:
with items as (
    select
        order_key,
        count(*) as item_count,
        sum(extended_price) as gross_revenue,
        sum(net_revenue) as net_revenue
    from {{ ref('fct_order_items') }}
    group by order_key
)

select
    o.order_key,
    o.customer_key,
    c.region_name,
    o.order_status,
    o.order_date,
    o.priority,
    coalesce(i.item_count, 0) as item_count,
    coalesce(i.gross_revenue, 0) as gross_revenue,
    coalesce(i.net_revenue, 0) as net_revenue,
    o.loaded_at
from {{ ref('stg_orders') }} o
left join {{ ref('dim_customers') }} c on o.customer_key = c.customer_key
left join items i on o.order_key = i.order_key
patch.explanation: Fixed the join condition between stg_orders and dim_customers. The original model incorrectly joined on o.order_key = c.customer_key, causing region_name to be null for most rows. Updated to the correct relationship o.customer_key = c.customer_key while preserving all other logic and column definitions.

output.evidence: not_null test on fct_orders.region_name failed with 14625 nulls out of 15000 rows. In fct_orders model, region_name is derived via left join to dim_customers using `on o.order_key = c.customer_key`. This join condition is incorrect; it should join on o.customer_key = c.customer_key. Query `select count(*) from staging.stg_orders o join marts.dim_customers c on o.order_key = c.customer_key` returned only 375 matches, leaving 14625 rows with null region_name. Upstream tables have correct row counts and no nulls, so the problem originates from the join logic in fct_orders model.

Updated to the correct relationship o.customer_key = c.customer_key while preserving all other logic and column definitions.
